'''François Taddei''' (born 5 August 1967) is a French [[geneticist]] and education researcher. Trained as an engineer, he worked on the [[Evolutionary genetics|evolutionary]] and medical [[Bacterial genetics|genetics of bacteria]] before turning to education. In 2006 he co-founded the ''Centre de Recherches Interdisciplinaires'' (CRI) with Ariel Lindner. The centre was renamed the [[Learning Planet Institute]] in 2021, and Taddei is its president.<ref name="lesechos2023">{{cite news |date=13 December 2023 |title=François Taddei croise les savoirs |trans-title=François Taddei brings knowledge together |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/services-conseils/francois-taddei-croise-les-savoirs-2073323 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251115083653/https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/services-conseils/francois-taddei-croise-les-savoirs-2073323 |archive-date=15 November 2025 |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Les Échos (France)|Les Échos]] |language=fr}}</ref> He has written or co-written several reports on the future of education, some of them commissioned by the [[Government of France|French government]].

== Early life ==
Taddei's father, Dominique Taddei, is an economist, a former university president and a former [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]] member of the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] for [[Vaucluse]]. His mother worked for a [[chamber of commerce]].<ref name="liberation2009">{{cite news |last=Bensimon |first=Corinne |date=14 April 2009 |title=Six milliards d'autodidactes |trans-title=Six billion self-taught learners |url=http://www.liberation.fr/sciences/0101561874-six-milliards-d-autodidactes |access-date=23 August 2020 |work=[[Libération]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref name="lesechos2023" /> The family is of [[Corsica|Corsican]] origin.<ref name="diepresse">{{cite news |last=Ahne |first=Verena |date=21 January 2014 |title=Wie ein Spiel: Wer forscht, der lernt |trans-title=Like a game: whoever does research learns |url=https://www.diepresse.com/1544743/wie-ein-spiel-wer-forscht-der-lernt |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Die Presse]] |language=de}}</ref> He went to school in [[Avignon]], where he won the [[Provence]] chess championship against adult players. At 15 he toured Italy by bicycle, and at 18 he travelled around Europe by train.<ref name="lesechos2023" /> During his national service he worked in military hospitals, where he became interested in biology.<ref name="lesechos2023" />

He arrived in [[New York City|New York]] for a research stay at [[Rockefeller University]] the day before the [[September 11 attacks]]. He has described that event, and the [[2005 French riots]], as the moments that led him towards civic engagement and education.<ref name="lesechos2023" /><ref name="lemonde20132" />

== Scientific career ==
Taddei graduated from the [[École polytechnique]] and is a chief engineer (''ingénieur général'') in the [[Corps of Bridges, Waters and Forests]]. He holds a doctorate in genetics, supervised by Croatian-French biologist [[Miroslav Radman]], and is a research director at [[Inserm]], the French National Institute of Health and Medical Research. At [[Paris Descartes University]] he led a team studying systems engineering and evolutionary dynamics, in particular how bacteria cooperate and [[Coevolution|coevolve]] in response to antibiotics. He has published in journals including ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|PNAS]]'' and ''[[PLOS]]''. In 2003 he and Radman jointly received the Inserm prize for fundamental research.<ref name="lemonde20132">{{cite news |last=Larousserie |first=David |date=27 March 2013 |title=François Taddei, chercheur interdiscipliné |trans-title=François Taddei, an interdisciplined researcher |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2013/03/21/francois-taddei-chercheur-interdiscipline_1852156_1650684.html |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr |issn=1950-6244}}</ref>

== Centre de Recherches Interdisciplinaires ==
In 2006 Taddei and Ariel Lindner, also an Inserm researcher, founded the CRI to bring researchers from different disciplines together. It was housed in a Paris Descartes University building opposite the [[Hôpital Cochin|Cochin Hospital]].<ref name="lemonde20132" /> According to Taddei, student numbers doubled every eighteen months, from about 80 in 2013 to 350 in 2019.<ref name="lemonde20132" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Vairet |first=Florent |date=19 February 2019 |title=Au CRI Paris, on pratique déjà le futur de l'apprentissage |trans-title=At the CRI in Paris, the future of learning is already in practice |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/politique-societe/education/au-cri-paris-on-pratique-deja-le-futur-de-lapprentissage-1175723 |work=[[Les Échos (France)|Les Échos]] |language=fr}}</ref> The French government's ''Investissements d'avenir'' ("Investments for the Future") programme provided additional funding for the centre's move to the [[Le Marais|Marais]] neighbourhood of Paris. The centre was later attached jointly to Paris Descartes, [[Paris Diderot University]] and [[Paris-Sorbonne University]] through the [[Sorbonne Paris Cité Alliance]].<ref>{{cite web |author=zecastor |date=12 November 2018 |title=Le CRI, centre créateur d'usages |trans-title=The CRI, a centre that creates new uses |url=https://www.journaldugeek.com/2018/11/12/cri-centre-createur-dusages/ |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=Journal du Geek |language=fr}}</ref>

In 2006 the researcher David Bikard joined Taddei's team to work on [[synthetic biology]], which ''[[Le Monde]]'' described as new in France. In 2008 a CRI team won the "fundamental research" prize at [[International Genetically Engineered Machine|iGEM]], an international competition run by the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), with €33,000 raised from donors.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kahn |first=Annie |date=12 January 2008 |title=Un club scientifique pour créer de nouvelles formes de vie |trans-title=A science club to create new forms of life |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/planete/article/2008/01/12/un-club-scientifique-pour-creer-de-nouvelles-formes-de-vie_998763_3244.html |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr |issn=1950-6244}}</ref>

From 2011 Taddei worked with the Austrian physicist [[Stefan Thurner]], of the [[Santa Fe Institute]] and the [[Medical University of Vienna]], on learning through games. Their collaboration led to iGam4ER (International Game Competition for Education and Research), held in Paris. The two also designed an online university based on curiosity-driven learning. According to Austrian newspaper ''[[Die Presse]]'', the project drew interest from the [[United Nations]] but did not go ahead.<ref name="diepresse" /> Taddei also started a science project for pupils in a deprived suburb of Paris.<ref name="diepresse" />

In 2014 the CRI held an international conference on the links between research and teaching, attended by 25 academics from countries including China, the United Kingdom and Canada. The same year the CRI obtained a [[UNESCO]] chair in the learning sciences, which ''Le Monde'' described as focused on innovation in teaching.<ref name="lemonde2014">{{cite news |last=Baumard |first=Maryline |date=2 April 2014 |title=A Paris, un colloque explore des voies d'enseignement nouvelles pour la science |trans-title=In Paris, a conference explores new ways of teaching science |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/education/article/2014/04/02/a-paris-un-colloque-explore-des-voies-d-enseignement-nouvelles-pour-la-science_4394163_1473685.html |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr |issn=1950-6244}}</ref>

In 2021 the CRI became the Learning Planet Institute. Taddei is its president and holds the title of "chief exploration officer". Gaël Mainguy is the institute's director general.<ref name="lesechos2023" />

== Work in education ==
=== Advisory roles ===
Taddei has taken part in several working groups on research and higher education. They include "France 2025", a government foresight exercise; the [[European Commission]]'s work on creativity in education;<ref>{{cite web |title=François Taddei |url=https://u-paris.fr/festival-idees-paris/francois-taddei/ |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=Festival des idées Paris |publisher=Université Paris Cité |language=fr}}</ref> the national strategy for higher education; and the strategic board of [[France Université Numérique]], the French national [[Massive open online course|MOOC]] platform.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bastide |first=Emmanuelle |date=17 January 2014 |title=7 milliards de voisins: A quoi servent les MOOC ? |trans-title=7 billion neighbours: what are MOOCs for? |url=http://www.rfi.fr/emission/20140117-1-servent-mooc/ |access-date=23 August 2020 |website=[[Radio France Internationale]] |language=fr}}</ref> In 2012 the president of the [[French Economic, Social and Environmental Council]] appointed him to the last ''Haut Conseil de l'éducation'' (High Council for Education).<ref>{{cite web |date=4 April 2012 |title=L'expresso du 4 avril 2012 |url=http://www.cafepedagogique.net/lexpresso/Pages/2012/04/04042012Accueil.aspx |website=Le Café pédagogique |language=fr}}</ref>

=== Associations ===
Students from the interdisciplinary master's programme that Taddei founded created Science Ac', an association that has given hundreds of secondary school pupils holiday placements in [[Research laboratory|research laboratories]].<ref name="liberation2009" /> Taddei also helped launch Paris-Montagne, which organises laboratory visits for secondary school pupils.<ref name="lemonde20132" /><ref name="guardian2010">{{cite news |last=Davies |first=Lizzy |date=21 July 2010 |title=Paris stages 'festival of errors' to teach French schoolchildren how to think |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/jul/21/france-paris-festival-of-errors |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== Views on education ===
In 2010 Taddei criticised the French school system for its low tolerance of mistakes and the little room it gives pupils to ask questions.<ref name="guardian2010" /> He has proposed using [[citizen science]] and scientific discovery games to open research-based learning to a wider public.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 November 2011 |title=La nouvelle science des amateurs |trans-title=The new science of amateurs |url=http://www.internetactu.net/2011/11/30/la-nouvelle-science-des-amateurs/ |access-date=23 August 2020 |website=InternetActu.net |language=fr}}</ref> One example is the Savanturiers programme, which runs observation projects in schools, such as studies of how certain plants fold their leaves.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 November 2018 |title=Savanturiers: Science mentoring the French way |url=https://microbiologycommunity.nature.com/posts/41596-savanturiers-science-mentoring-the-french-way |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=Research Communities by Springer Nature}}</ref>

In his 2018 book ''Apprendre au XXIe siècle'' ("Learning in the 21st century"), Taddei argues that learning works by stabilising random neural connections, a process he presents as common to all types of cells. He also argues that education systems have not prepared for the changes brought by [[artificial intelligence]] (AI), and calls for more research and development spending in education.<ref name="lesechos2018">{{cite news |date=28 September 2018 |title=Mieux apprendre, ça s'apprend |trans-title=Learning better can be learned |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/2018/09/mieux-apprendre-ca-sapprend-1120998 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605163531/https://www.lesechos.fr/2018/09/mieux-apprendre-ca-sapprend-1120998 |archive-date=5 June 2023 |access-date=25 September 2026 |work=[[Les Échos (France)|Les Échos]] |language=fr}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==

* 2003: Inserm prize for fundamental research, shared with Miroslav Radman<ref name="lemonde20132" />
* 2004: [[Liliane Bettencourt Prize for Life Sciences]], for research on the evolution and ageing of bacteria<ref>{{cite web |title=Sciences de la vie |url=http://www.fondationbs.org/C_les_programmes/C1_medical/C1_B_prix/#aller2003 |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=Fondation Bettencourt Schueller |language=fr}}</ref>
* 2005: European Young Investigator Award (EURYI), for research on the evolution and ageing of bacteria<ref name="lemonde20132" />
* 2006: [[Human Frontier Science Program]] award{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* 2013: Knight of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques]]{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* 2017: Prix [[Montgolfier brothers|Montgolfier]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Liste des lauréats Montgolfier |url=https://www.calameo.com/read/003517961095d165c85ef |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=Calaméo |language=fr}}</ref>
* 2018: Knight of the [[Ordre des Arts et des Lettres]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Nomination dans l'ordre des Arts et des Lettres – été 2018 |url=https://www.culture.gouv.fr/Nous-connaitre/Organisation/Conseil-de-l-Ordre-des-Arts-et-des-Lettres/Arretes-de-Nominations-dans-l-ordre-des-Arts-et-des-Lettres/Nomination-dans-l-ordre-des-Arts-et-des-Lettres-ete-2018 |website=culture.gouv.fr |publisher=Ministry of Culture |language=fr}}</ref>
* 2019: Prix Eurêka<ref>{{cite web |title=Prix Eurêka: lauréats 2019 |url=https://www.amcsti.fr/fr/actions/prix-eureka/ |website=AMCSTI |language=fr}}</ref>
* 2020: Honorary doctorate from [[UCLouvain]]<ref>{{cite web |date=4 February 2020 |title=François Taddei, la bio express |url=https://www.lesoir.be/277664/article/2020-02-04/francois-taddei-la-bio-express |access-date=25 September 2026 |website=[[Le Soir]] |language=fr}}</ref>
